title: DC Generators — Types, Equations & Parallel Operation
subtitle: DC generators convert mechanical rotation into DC electricity. The key differences between types are how they supply their own field current — this determines their voltage-load characteristics. Every type uses the same core equation V = E − IaRa.
learningOutcome: DC generators convert mechanical rotation into DC electricity. The key differences between types are how they supply their own field current — this determines their voltage-load characteristics. Every type uses the same core equation V = E − IaRa.

content.text: Core equation for all generators: V = E − IaRa. Terminal voltage V is always less than generated EMF E because Ra drops some voltage.
Generator types — field connection and current equations

Exam-ready — four conditions for parallel operation:
(1) Terminal voltages must be equal. (2) Polarities must be the same (+to+, −to−). (3) Prime movers must have similar stable speed-load characteristics. (4) The rate of change of voltage with load must be of the same order for all generators.

Common mistake — In a shunt generator, Ia = IL + If (armature supplies both load AND field). Forgetting If makes Ra wrong. Always draw the circuit and identify all current branches before writing any equation.
